proofs.proof_tex:
By the definition of \(h\), \(h(0)=0\), so \(g(0)=0\).  The definition of \(J_n\) therefore gives, for every realized selected vector,
\[
 \mathcal R_{jn}=J_n(0)-J_n(\widehat\beta_{jn})
 =\lambda\{g(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2)-g(0)\}
 =\lambda g(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2).
\]
Differentiating the displayed definition of \(h\) gives
\[
 h'(z)=\sigma(z)+z\sigma'(z)-\sigma(z)=z\sigma'(z).
\]
For \(r\) in a bounded interval, \(|Z h'(rZ)|\le rZ^2/4\), which is integrable under the Gaussian-feature assumption.  Dominated differentiation thus yields
\[
 g'(r)=\mathbb E\{Zh'(rZ)\}
       =r\mathbb E\{Z^2\sigma'(rZ)\}.
\]
Since \(\sigma'(z)=\sigma(z)\{1-\sigma(z)\}>0\) and \(\mathbb P(Z\ne0)=1\), this derivative is strictly positive for every \(r>0\).

It remains to prove the distributional assertion for method \(T\).  The logistic identity \(\sigma(-z)=1-\sigma(z)\) implies that \(\sigma(z)-1/2\) is odd.  Direct substitution in the definition of \(h\) also gives \(h(-z)=h(z)\).  Since \(q_{ni}=S_{ni}X_{ni}\), for every \(\beta\in\mathcal B_n\), simultaneously,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F_{Tn}(\beta)
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left[2S_{ni}Y_{ni}\{\sigma(S_{ni}X_{ni}^{\top}\beta)-1/2\}
       -\lambda h(S_{ni}X_{ni}^{\top}\beta)\right]\\
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left[2Y_{ni}\{\sigma(X_{ni}^{\top}\beta)-1/2\}
       -\lambda h(X_{ni}^{\top}\beta)\right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
By randomization and central symmetry of the Gaussian law, for every Borel set \(B\subset\mathbb R^{p_n}\) and \(s\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 \mathbb P(X_{ni}\in B,S_{ni}=s)
 =\tfrac12\mathbb P(sq_{ni}\in B)
 =\tfrac12\mathbb P(q_{ni}\in B).
\]
Hence \(X_{ni}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{p_n})\) and \(X_{ni}\) is independent of \(S_{ni}\).  Conditional on \(X_{ni}=x\), the outcome assumption and the preceding independence give
\[
 \mathbb P(Y_{ni}=1\mid X_{ni}=x)
 =\tfrac12\sigma(\gamma x_1)+\tfrac12\sigma(-\gamma x_1)=\tfrac12.
\]
Thus \(Y_{ni}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(Y_{ni}\) is independent of \(X_{ni}\).  Independence across observations follows from the row independence and conditional outcome independence assumptions.  Consequently the entire random function in the last display has the law generated by independent \(X_{ni}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{p_n})\) and \(Y_{ni}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), a law containing no \(\gamma\).  The global selector is a deterministic function of this random function, so its selected norm and the radial regret have gamma-free marginal laws.  This argument conditions neither on the original \(Q_n\) nor on the assignments and makes no assertion about any joint law involving entropy tilts, method \(E\), method \(D\), or cross-method branch quantities.

Fix an arm \(a\), condition on its index set \(I_{an}=\{i:A_{ni}=a\}\), and write \(m=|I_{an}|\) and \(\alpha_m=m/n\).  The exceptional cases \(m\in\{0,n\}\) have probability tending to zero under randomization.  For one feature coordinate, the vector of centered arm rows
\[
 C^{(\ell)}=(q_{ni,\ell}-\bar q_{n,\ell}:i\in I_{an})^{\top}
\]
is centered Gaussian and has covariance
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(C^{(\ell)}_i,C^{(\ell)}_k)
 =\mathbf 1\{i=k\}-\frac1n.
\]
Different feature coordinates remain independent.  With \(u=m^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_m\), define
\[
 \Sigma_m=I_m-\alpha_m uu^{\top},\qquad
 A_m=\Sigma_m^{1/2}=I_m-c_muu^{\top},\qquad
 c_m=1-\sqrt{1-\alpha_m}.
\]
Because \(0<\alpha_m<1\), \(A_m\) is invertible.  The centered arm matrix \(C_m\) therefore has the distribution
\[
 C_m=A_mG_m,qquad G_m\in\mathbb R^{m\times p_n}
 \text{ with independent }\mathcal N(0,1)\text{ entries}.
\]

A finite convex combination represents \(\bar q_n\) as a relative-interior point of the arm hull if and only if it can be represented with every coefficient strictly positive.  Indeed, every strictly positive combination is in the relative interior.  Conversely, average all arm points to obtain a relative-interior point \(z\); if \(y\) is in the relative interior, then for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), \(y'=(y-\varepsilon z)/(1-\varepsilon)\) remains in the hull, and \(y=(1-\varepsilon)y'+\varepsilon z\) has a representation with all coefficients positive.  Applying this equivalence to \(y=\bar q_n\) shows that
\[
 \mathcal E_{an}quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \ker(G_m^{\top})\cap\operatorname{int}(K_m)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad K_m=A_m\mathbb R_+^m,
\]
apart from the already excluded empty-arm case.  The nullspace of the independent Gaussian matrix is Haar distributed on the Grassmannian.  To compare interior and closed-cone intersection, put \(B_m=G_m^{\top}A_m\).  Almost surely, simultaneously for every column set \(I\), the submatrix \((B_m)_I\) has rank \(\min(p_n,|I|)\): each such submatrix has a nonsingular Gaussian row covariance because every principal submatrix of \(A_m^2=\Sigma_m\) is positive definite, and there are only finitely many \(I\).  Suppose \(B_mw=0\) for a nonzero \(w\ge0\), and let \(I=\{i:w_i>0\}\).  Full column rank rules out \(|I|\le p_n\), so \(|I|>p_n\) and \((B_m)_I\) has full row rank.  For each \(j\notin I\), choose \(v^{(j)}_I\) solving \((B_m)_Iv^{(j)}_I=-(B_m)_j\), put \(v^{(j)}_j=1\), and put its other coordinates outside \(I\) equal to zero.  Then \(B_mv^{(j)}=0\).  Choosing all positive coefficients \(\varepsilon_j\) sufficiently small makes
\[
 w'=w+\sum_{j\notin I}\varepsilon_jv^{(j)}
\]
strictly positive while preserving \(B_mw'=0\).  Thus closed-cone intersection implies interior intersection almost surely; the converse is immediate.  Hence the last event agrees almost surely with
\[
 \ker(G_m^{\top})\cap K_m\ne\{0\}.
\]

We next calculate the statistical dimension of \(K_m\).  Let \(G=(G_1,\ldots,G_m)^{\top}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_m)\).  By the cited metric characterization, projection onto \(K_m\) is obtained by minimizing \(\|G-A_mw\|_2^2\) over \(w\ge0\).  Since \(A_m^{\top}A_m=\Sigma_m\), the coordinate Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, which are sufficient because this quadratic is strictly convex, are
\[
 w_i=\bigl(G_i-c_m\bar G+t_m\bigr)_+,qquad
 t_m=\alpha_m\overline w
     =\alpha_m\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m
       \bigl(G_i-c_m\bar G+t_m\bigr)_+.
\]
The right side of the scalar fixed-point equation is Lipschitz in \(t_m\) with constant at most \(\alpha_m<1\), so the solution is unique.  If \(\alpha_m\to\alpha\in(0,1)\), the law of large numbers, \(\bar G\to0\), and the contraction bound imply
\[
 t_m\longrightarrow t_\alpha,qquad
 t_\alpha=\alpha H(t_\alpha),qquad
 H(t)=\mathbb E(G_1+t)_+=\phi(t)+t\Phi(t).
\]
The root is unique and positive because the derivative of \(\alpha H(t)-t\) is \(\alpha\Phi(t)-1<0\), its value at zero is \(\alpha\phi(0)>0\), and it tends to minus infinity as \(t\to\infty\).

For the minimizing \(w\),
\[
 \frac1m\|\Pi_{K_m}(G)\|_2^2
 =\frac1m w^{\top}\Sigma_mw
 =\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^mw_i^2-\alpha_m\overline w^{,2}.
\]
The same law-of-large-numbers argument gives convergence in probability of the right side to
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E(G_1+t_\alpha)_+^2-\alpha H(t_\alpha)^2
 &=(1+t_\alpha^2)\Phi(t_\alpha)+t_\alpha\phi(t_\alpha)
   -t_\alpha H(t_\alpha)\\
 &=\Phi(t_\alpha),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the fixed-point equation was used in the first line.  Projection contraction gives \(\|\Pi_{K_m}(G)\|_2^2/m\le\|G\|_2^2/m\), and \(\mathbb E(\|G\|_2^2/m)^2=1+2/m\).  Uniform integrability and the cited metric characterization therefore yield
\[
 \frac{\delta(K_m)}m\longrightarrow\Phi(t_\alpha).
\]

Assume now that \(p_n/m\to\kappa/\alpha\).  A fixed subspace of dimension \(m-p_n\) has statistical dimension \(m-p_n\), because the expected squared norm of the projection of a standard Gaussian vector onto it is \(m-p_n\).  Thus
\[
 \delta(K_m)+(m-p_n)-m
 =m\left\{\Phi(t_\alpha)-\frac\kappa\alpha\right\}+o(m).
\]
For any fixed separation from \(\kappa=\alpha\Phi(t_\alpha)\), this quantity has magnitude of order \(m\), and hence eventually dominates the \(a_\eta\sqrt m\) transition width in the cited approximate kinematic formula.  Letting the fixed tolerance \(\eta\downarrow0\) proves conditional feasibility probability tending to one below \(\alpha\Phi(t_\alpha)\), and tending to zero above it.

By Chebyshev's inequality applied to the independent treatment indicators, \(n_{an}/n\to1/2\) in probability for both arms.  The preceding deterministic-sequence argument is uniform over counts in a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(n/2\): otherwise a countersequence of counts would contradict the proved limit.  Removing the conditioning and using a union bound consequently gives
\[
 \mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n})\to1
 \quad\text{if }\kappa<\tfrac12\Phi(t_{1/2}),
\]
and in fact \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cup\mathcal E_{1n})\to0\) if \(\kappa>\tfrac12\Phi(t_{1/2})\).  Since \(\kappa<1/2\), eventually \(p_n<n\); the Gaussian matrix \(Q_n\) then has column rank \(p_n\) almost surely, so adjoining \(\mathcal Q_n\) does not alter the first limit.

Finally, when \(\alpha=1/2\), the scalar equation is exactly
\[
 t_{\mathrm{bal}}=\{\phi(t_{\mathrm{bal}})+t_{\mathrm{bal}}\Phi(t_{\mathrm{bal}})\}/2,
 \qquad \kappa_{\mathrm{bal}}=\Phi(t_{\mathrm{bal}})/2.
\]
Monotonicity already proves uniqueness.  Direct interval evaluation gives
\(0.2760298047<t_{\mathrm{bal}}<0.2760298049\) and
\(0.304368706413<\Phi(t_{\mathrm{bal}})/2<0.304368706453\), which establishes the displayed decimal.  On the joint event, extend \(w\log(n_{an}w)\) continuously by zero at \(w=0\).  The feasible simplex is compact, so a minimizer exists, and strict convexity makes it unique.  If this minimizer had a zero coordinate, moving toward the strictly positive feasible vector established above would have directional derivative minus infinity because \(t\log t\) has that derivative at zero; this contradicts minimality.  The minimizer is therefore strictly positive, the equality-constrained Lagrange equations give the exponential-tilt form, and the stipulated minimum-norm rule resolves any dual nonidentifiability.  Thus both arms use their unique exact-balancing entropy solutions.  Finally, \(\mathcal Q_n\) gives the ordinary inverse formula for the full-sample resolvent.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and put \(a_\eta=\sqrt{8\log(4/\eta)}\).  If \(C,K\subset\mathbb R^d\) are closed convex cones, \(U\) is Haar orthogonal, and \(\delta(\cdot)\) denotes statistical dimension, then
\[
 \delta(C)+\delta(K)\le d-a_\eta\sqrt d
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb P\{C\cap UK\ne\{0\}\}\le\eta,
\]
whereas
\[
 \delta(C)+\delta(K)\ge d+a_\eta\sqrt d
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb P\{C\cap UK\ne\{0\}\}\ge1-\eta.
\]

attestation.note: Checked against arXiv:1303.6672v2, Theorem I; the stable arXiv handle is supplied in lieu of a long verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every closed convex cone \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\), its statistical dimension satisfies
\[
 \delta(C)=\mathbb E\|\Pi_C(G)\|_2^2,
 \qquad G\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),
\]
where \(\Pi_C\) is Euclidean projection onto \(C\).

attestation.note: Checked against arXiv:1303.6672v2, Proposition 2.4; the stable arXiv handle is supplied in lieu of a long verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement:
On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), exact pooled-target balance implies
\[
 Q_n^{\top}d_n=0
\]
and, conditionally on \(Q_n\) and \((A_{ni})_{i=1}^n\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\mid Q_n,(A_{ni})_{i=1}^n\right]
 =\|L_nD_nu_n\|_2^2+
   \operatorname{tr}(L_nD_nV_nD_nL_n^{\top}).
\]
On this event \(L_n=(Q_n^{\top}Q_n)^{-1}Q_n^{\top}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nn})^{\top}\) and \(Y_n=(Y_{n1},\ldots,Y_{nn})^{\top}\).  On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\), the two arm weight vectors each sum to one and each balance to \(\bar q_n\).  Since \(S_{ni}=1\) in arm one and \(S_{ni}=-1\) in arm zero, the definition \(d_{ni}=nS_{ni}w_{iA_{ni}n}\) gives
\[
 Q_n^{\top}d_n
 =n\left\{\sum_{i:A_{ni}=1}w_{i1n}q_{ni}
           -\sum_{i:A_{ni}=0}w_{i0n}q_{ni}\right\}
 =n(\bar q_n-\bar q_n)=0.
\]
Conditionally on \(Q_n\) and the assignments, the weights and hence \(D_n\) are fixed.  Put \(\varepsilon_n=Y_n-m_n\), where \(m_n=(m_{n1},\ldots,m_{nn})^{\top}\).  The binary-outcome assumption gives
\[
 \mathbb E(\varepsilon_n\mid Q_n,A_n)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(\varepsilon_n\varepsilon_n^{\top}\mid Q_n,A_n)=V_n,
\]
because the outcomes are conditionally independent.  Since \(Y_n-\mathbf1_n/2=u_n+\varepsilon_n\),
\[
 b_{E,n}=L_nD_nu_n+L_nD_n\varepsilon_n.
\]
Expanding its squared norm, the cross term has conditional expectation zero, and the quadratic term satisfies \(\mathbb E(\varepsilon_n^{\top}B\varepsilon_n\mid Q_n,A_n)=\operatorname{tr}(BV_n)\) with \(B=D_nL_n^{\top}L_nD_n\).  Cyclicity of trace proves the claimed identity.  Finally, on \(\mathcal Q_n\), \(Q_n^{\top}Q_n\) is invertible, so the Moore--Penrose expression in the definition of \(L_n\) equals \((Q_n^{\top}Q_n)^{-1}Q_n^{\top}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose the feature dimension \(p\) is fixed and \(n\to\infty\).  For each fixed bulk coordinate \(k\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\), the coordinate influences of the empirical gradient at \(\beta=0\) for true-propensity IPW, exact entropy-balanced IPW, and oracle DR are respectively
\[
 \psi_{T,k}=\tfrac12SYq_k,qquad
 \psi_{E,k}=\tfrac12S\bigl[\{Y-\tfrac12\}q_k-\mu_k\bigr],
 \qquad
 \psi_{D,k}=\tfrac12S\{Y-m(q)\}q_k,
\]
where \(\mu=\mathbb E\{m(q)q\}\) and \(\mu_k=0\) for \(k>1\).  Their variances are
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{T,k})=\frac18,qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{E,k})=\frac1{16},qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{D,k})=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n)\to1\) in this fixed-dimensional regime.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
At \(\beta=0\), \(\sigma'(0)=1/4\) and \(h'(0)=0\).  Therefore one observation contributes \(\psi_T=SYq/2\) to the true-IPW gradient and \(\psi_D=S(Y-m(q))q/2\) to the oracle-DR gradient.  For a bulk coordinate \(k>1\), \(q_k\) is independent of \(q_1\), \(\mathbb E m(q)=1/2\) by \(m(-q_1)=1-m(q_1)\), and randomization makes \(S\) conditionally mean zero.  Hence both influences have mean zero and
\[
 \mathbb E\psi_{T,k}^2
 =\tfrac14\mathbb E(Yq_k^2)=\tfrac18,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\psi_{D,k}^2
 =\tfrac14\mathbb E[m(q)\{1-m(q)\}q_k^2]=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]

For entropy balancing, let \(\bar q_a\) and \(\overline{Yq}_a\) denote the unweighted arm means.  At zero tilt, the derivative of the exponentially tilted arm mean of \(q\) is its sample covariance, which converges to \(I_p\).  A fixed-dimensional Taylor expansion of the exact balance equation therefore gives
\[
 \eta_{an}=\bar q_n-\bar q_a+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Let \(M_a=\sum_{i:A_{ni}=a}w_{ian}Y_{ni}q_{ni}\).  The derivative at zero tilt of the corresponding weighted mean of \(Yq\) is
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Yq,q)
 =\mathbb E\{m(q)qq^{\top}\}=\tfrac12I_p.
\]
The last equality follows by pairing \(q_1\) with \(-q_1\): \(qq^{\top}\) is unchanged for diagonal and off-signal bulk entries, the remaining odd cross entries integrate to zero, and \(m(q_1)+m(-q_1)=1\).  Thus
\[
 M_a-\mu=\overline{Yq}_a-\mu+  frac12(\bar q_n-\bar q_a)+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For any square-integrable vector \(f\) with mean \(\nu\), the arm ratio obeys the direct expansion
\[
 \frac{\mathbb P_n\{\mathbf1(A=a)f\}}{\mathbb P_n\{\mathbf1(A=a)\}}-\nu
 =2\mathbb P_n[\mathbf1(A=a)(f-\nu)]+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
because \(\mathbb P_n\{\mathbf1(A=a)\}=1/2+O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) and the centered numerator is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\).  Applying this identity to the two sample means shows that the one-observation influence of \(M_a\) is
\[
 2\mathbf1\{A=a\}(Yq-\mu)+  frac12\{q-2\mathbf1\{A=a\}q\}.
\]
The entropy-balanced gradient is \((M_1-M_0)/4\).  Subtracting the two arm influences and using \(S=2A-1\) gives
\[
 \psi_E=\tfrac12S\bigl[\{Y-  frac12\}q-\mu\bigr].
\]
Symmetry gives \(\mu_k=0\) for \(k>1\).  Since a binary \(Y\) obeys \((Y-1/2)^2=1/4\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{E,k})
 =\tfrac14\mathbb E[\{Y-  frac12\}^2q_k^2]=\frac1{16}.
\]

For completeness, fixed-dimensional strict feasibility follows directly from full support of the Gaussian law.  Choose \(p+1\) deterministic vertices whose simplex contains a neighborhood of zero.  Small neighborhoods of those vertices retain this property and each has positive probability in each randomized arm.  With probability tending to one every such neighborhood is represented in both arms; simultaneously \(\bar q_n\to0\), so \(\bar q_n\) lies in the interior of each arm hull.  Gaussian absolute continuity also gives \(\operatorname{rank}(Q_n)=p\) almost surely once \(n\ge p\).  This proves the event assertion and validates the tilt expansions on an event whose probability tends to one.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly for \(\gamma\) in compact subsets of \((\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma)\),
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma)\ \Rightarrow\ 
 \mathcal N(0,I_\gamma^{-1}),
 \qquad
 I_\gamma=\mathbb E[Z^2\sigma(\gamma Z)\{1-\sigma(\gamma Z)\}]>0,
\]
and \(\widehat I_{\gamma,n}\to_{\mathbb P}I_\gamma\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For one observation, apart from terms not depending on \(g\), the log likelihood is
\[
 \ell_i(g)=Y_{ni}gq_{ni,1}-\log\{1+\exp(gq_{ni,1})\}.
\]
Its first two derivatives are
\[
 \dot\ell_i(g)=q_{ni,1}\{Y_{ni}-\sigma(gq_{ni,1})\},
 \qquad
 \ddot\ell_i(g)=-q_{ni,1}^2\sigma(gq_{ni,1})\{1-\sigma(gq_{ni,1})\}.
\]
At the true \(\gamma\), the score has conditional mean zero and variance \(I_\gamma\).  The information is strictly positive because its integrand is positive whenever \(Z\ne0\).  The expected log likelihood is uniquely maximized at \(\gamma\): equivalently, its difference from the value at \(\gamma\) is the negative expectation of the Bernoulli Kullback--Leibler divergence, with equality only when \(\sigma(gZ)=\sigma(\gamma Z)\) almost surely, hence only when \(g=\gamma\).  Gaussian moments dominate the likelihood derivatives uniformly on the compact parameter interval.  Uniform laws of large numbers therefore give consistency of every maximizer and uniform convergence of the empirical negative Hessian near \(\gamma\) to \(I_\gamma\).  The mean-value expansion of the score equation, together with the ordinary central limit theorem, yields
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma)
 =I_\gamma^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 q_{ni,1}\{Y_{ni}-m_{ni}\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,I_\gamma^{-1}).
\]
The same envelope argument, consistency, and a uniform law of large numbers applied to the displayed definition of \(\widehat I_{\gamma,n}\) prove information consistency.  All bounds are uniform when \(\gamma\) ranges over a compact subset of the interior.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\xi_n^0=(p_n/n,\gamma,\lambda,R)\), \(\widehat d_n=d(\widehat\xi_n)\), and \(I_\gamma=\mathbb E[Z^2\sigma(\gamma Z)\{1-\sigma(\gamma Z)\}]\).  On every compact set \(K\subset(0,\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}})\times(\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma)\times(0,\infty)^2\) on which the four-distance map is continuously differentiable and
\[
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\min\{d_{\mathrm{bal}}(\xi),d_{\mathrm{rad}}(\xi),d_{\mathrm{col}}(\xi),d_0(\xi)\}>0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty>0,
\]
uniformly in \(\xi\in K\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat d_n-d(\xi_n^0)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_4\!\left(0,\Omega(\xi)\right),\qquad
 \Omega(\xi)=\frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma},\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_n\to_{\mathbb P}\Omega(\xi).
\]
Consequently, the simultaneous intervals \([\widehat d_{\ell n}-\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha},\widehat d_{\ell n}+\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha}]\), \(\ell\in\{\mathrm{bal},\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{col},0\}\), have joint coverage at least \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly on \(K\), and
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in K}\mathbb P_\xi\{\widehat s_{n,\alpha}\ne\operatorname{sgn}(\Delta_{\mathrm{HIR}}(\xi))\}\to0,
\]
where abstention counts as an error.  Thus the classifier is total, reports \(\bot\) whenever a certificate is missing or an estimated boundary distance fails to exceed \(\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha}\), and is uniformly nonabstaining and sign-consistent on compact margin-separated, derivative-nondegenerate sets.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current Gaussian-max radius is exactly zero if every gamma derivative vanishes. Weak convergence to a point mass then does not imply coverage by zero-width intervals. Uniform derivative nondegeneracy is therefore necessary for the stated quantile-based coverage conclusion; this narrows only the regular inference regime and does not assume the unresolved joint-system crux.

proposed.statement: Let \(t_{\mathrm{bal}}\) solve \(t=\{\phi(t)+t\Phi(t)\}/2\) and let \(\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}}=\Phi(t_{\mathrm{bal}})/2=0.3043687064\ldots\). Then \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n)\to1\) when \(\kappa<\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}}\), while \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n})\to0\) when \(\kappa>\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}}\). In the interior regime, \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\) is therefore the certified event on which both arms use their unique exact-balancing entropy solutions and the ordinary full-rank leverage identities apply.
proposed.justification: The theorem identifies the exact domain on which proportional exact entropy balancing exists.
proposed.gap: ZhaoPercival2017 gives fixed-dimensional interiority and DaiYan2024 documents high-dimensional infeasibility; neither derives the endogenous pooled-target threshold.
proposed.consumer: The threshold tells trial analysts when exact same-coordinate balancing is mathematically unavailable before any policy comparison is attempted.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the two published conic-geometry facts used by the proof into the theorem's declared proof spine.

proposed.statement: Write \(A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nn})^{\top}\). On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the unique exact-balancing weights imply \(Q_n^{\top}d_n=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\mid Q_n,A_n]=\|L_nD_nu_n\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(L_nD_nV_nD_nL_n^{\top})\), with \(L_n=(Q_n^\top Q_n)^{-1}Q_n^\top\) on this event. At \(\gamma=1\), on the same certified event, the two terms and their covariance corrections admit deterministic resolvent limits under the original same-sample entropy weights on an interval containing \(\kappa=1/8\), and the resulting limit recovers \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\) as \(\kappa\downarrow0\). No identity or entropy-balance conclusion is asserted for the uniform fallback on the complement.
proposed.justification: This is the early kill test for whether coherent leverage and Jacobian terms have a finite closure.
proposed.gap: LuYangWang2025 controls proportional linear and quadratic leverage for regression adjustment, but the diagonal weights here are endogenous exponential tilts sharing the same Gaussian rows.
proposed.consumer: Passing this test validates the strong-penalty benchmark required to trust any full phase diagram.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved finite-sample conditional identity into the still-open proportional deterministic-equivalent target.

proposed.statement: Under the same one-observation law with \(p_n=p\) fixed before \(n\to\infty\), the true-propensity IPW and oracle DR bulk-coordinate gradient variances at \(\beta=0\) are \(1/8\) and \(v_\gamma/4\), respectively. On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the exact linear entropy-balance variance is \(1/16\); this event has probability tending to one in the fixed-dimensional limit. Consequently, as \(\kappa\downarrow0\) after the proportional limits, \(r_T=\kappa/(4\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), and \(r_D=v_\gamma\kappa/(2\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), provided the certified-event uniform remainder asserted by the joint system holds. The uniform complement-event fallback is not identified with entropy balancing in this reduction.
proposed.justification: This sanity reduction anchors the proportional system to the classical HIR projection while showing that linear balance remains strictly short of oracle DR when the signal is positive.
proposed.gap: HiranoImbensRidder2003 and FangRidderXie2026 obtain full efficiency from sufficiently rich estimated propensity scores; the exact same-coordinate linear balance used here spans only a partial projection.
proposed.consumer: The reduction gives analysts a low-dimensional diagnostic and prevents interpreting exact linear balance as automatic oracle efficiency.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved fixed-dimensional entropy-score projection and all three bulk-coordinate variances into the target's declared proof spine.

proposed.statement:
Let \(\xi_n^0=(p_n/n,\gamma,\lambda,R)\), \(\widehat d_n=d(\widehat\xi_n)\), and \(I_\gamma=\mathbb E[Z^2\sigma(\gamma Z)\{1-\sigma(\gamma Z)\}]\).  On every compact set \(K\subset(0,\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}})\times(\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma)\times(0,\infty)^2\) on which the four-distance map is continuously differentiable and
\[
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\min\{d_{\mathrm{bal}}(\xi),d_{\mathrm{rad}}(\xi),d_{\mathrm{col}}(\xi),d_0(\xi)\}>0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty>0,
\]
uniformly in \(\xi\in K\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat d_n-d(\xi_n^0)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_4\!\left(0,\Omega(\xi)\right),\qquad
 \Omega(\xi)=\frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma},\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_n\to_{\mathbb P}\Omega(\xi).
\]
Consequently, the simultaneous intervals \([\widehat d_{\ell n}-\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha},\widehat d_{\ell n}+\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha}]\), \(\ell\in\{\mathrm{bal},\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{col},0\}\), have joint coverage at least \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly on \(K\), and
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in K}\mathbb P_\xi\{\widehat s_{n,\alpha}\ne\operatorname{sgn}(\Delta_{\mathrm{HIR}}(\xi))\}\to0,
\]
where abstention counts as an error.  Thus the classifier is total, reports \(\bot\) whenever a certificate is missing or an estimated boundary distance fails to exceed \(\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha}\), and is uniformly nonabstaining and sign-consistent on compact margin-separated, derivative-nondegenerate sets.
proposed.justification: A deterministic diagram is operational only if its phase label can be learned from a trial away from nonregular boundaries.
proposed.gap: SurCandes2019 estimates scalar states for one logistic MLE and LuYangWang2025 estimates quadratic variance components; neither gives joint inference for a contrast of dependent optimized policy criteria.
proposed.consumer: The theorem supplies an uncertainty-aware label for whether entropy balancing improves or worsens targeting regret in a feature-expanded trial reanalysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Apply the proposed regularity narrowing and wire the proved scalar signal-estimation limit into the inference theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A deterministic equivalent for the two endogenous same-sample entropy-weighted resolvent terms at signal one, including their conditional concentration and the uniform small-aspect-ratio link to fixed-penalty regret.
open_obligations.obstruction: The diagonal entropy weights and the least-squares resolvent are functions of the same Gaussian rows. The frozen assumptions provide neither a leave-one-out response theorem nor weighted-leverage bounds strong enough to replace these objects by marginal tilt moments.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact balance cancellation and conditional Bernoulli decomposition were completed. A marginal-weight or independent-weight substitution was rejected because it drops nonvanishing coherent leverage terms and changes the estimator.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Write \(A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nn})^{\top}\). The finite-sample part is proved exactly: on the certified event,
\[
 Q_n^{\top}d_n=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\mid Q_n,A_n\right]
 =\|L_nD_nu_n\|_2^2+
 \operatorname{tr}(L_nD_nV_nD_nL_n^{\top}),
\]
and \(L_n=(Q_n^{\top}Q_n)^{-1}Q_n^{\top}\).  This identity retains both the coherent conditional-mean term and the endogenous weighted-leverage trace.  No deterministic equivalent for either same-sample term has been established from the frozen assumptions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construction and proof of a finite deterministic same-sample tilt-policy resolvent system with global, rather than merely stationary, selection for all three nonconcave policy objectives.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact first-order equations retain two entropy tilts, all tilt-policy overlaps, and the block-Jacobian response to reuse of every row. The empirical policy criterion is not globally concave in the logistic coefficient, so a stationary fixed point cannot certify the selected global norm or exclude branch coexistence.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact finite-sample balance and policy KKT equations, the conic feasibility phase, the radial regret reduction, and the strong-penalty conditional identity were derived. Convex Gaussian minimax and independent-weight surrogates were rejected because their hypotheses or estimators differ from the frozen construction.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Define \(\mathbb P_nf=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i\).  The exact finite-sample necessary equations on the certified event are, with \(W_{ian}=nw_{ian}\),
\[
 \mathbb P_n[\mathbf1\{A_{ni}=a\}W_{ian}]=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_n[\mathbf1\{A_{ni}=a\}W_{ian}q_{ni}]=\bar q_n,
\]
and, for any differentiable constrained policy maximizer, there is \(\tau_{jn}\ge0\) such that
\[
 \mathbb P_n\!\left[q_{ni}\sigma'(q_{ni}^{\top}\widehat\beta_{jn})
 \{c_{j,ni}-\lambda q_{ni}^{\top}\widehat\beta_{jn}\}\right]
 =\tau_{jn}\widehat\beta_{jn},
 \quad
 \tau_{jn}(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2^2-R^2)=0.
\]
The radial proposition proves that any eventual deterministic norm limits would imply \(r_j=\lambda g(\rho_j)\) and would determine the HIR sign by comparing \(\rho_T\) and \(\rho_E\).  These necessary equations do not certify global optimality of the nonconcave objective and do not close the same-sample tilt-policy response terms.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The certified branch map, its derivatives, and their uniform plug-in consistency, all of which depend on resolving the joint deterministic system.
open_obligations.obstruction: The scalar signal estimator has a regular limit, but the frozen handle supplies no explicit state equations or proved globally selected branch to differentiate. The original coverage claim also omits derivative nondegeneracy and can use a zero-width critical radius.
open_obligations.attempted: The logistic score expansion, information consistency, and the conditional delta-method covariance were derived. A statement narrowing adds the minimal derivative nondegeneracy needed by the defined Gaussian-max quantile, without assuming the unresolved optimizer theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The scalar statistical component is closed: uniformly on compact subsets of the interior signal interval,
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,I_\gamma^{-1}),
 \qquad \widehat I_{\gamma,n}\to_{\mathbb P}I_\gamma.
\]
If a certified branch supplied a continuously differentiable distance map, the delta-method covariance would be \(\partial_\gamma d\,\partial_\gamma d^{\top}/I_\gamma\).  The frozen joint system does not yet supply that branch or its derivatives.  In addition, positive simultaneous-radius coverage requires the stated derivative nondegeneracy; otherwise the defined Gaussian-max radius can be exactly zero.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform control that permits taking the proportional deterministic limit first and then sending the aspect ratio to zero for the original same-sample entropy estimator.
open_obligations.obstruction: Fixed-dimensional asymptotic linearity controls each fixed number of coordinates but does not control the sum of a growing number of coordinate errors. The needed uniform remainder is part of the unresolved joint system and cannot be inferred from the frozen assumptions.
open_obligations.attempted: All three fixed-dimensional influence functions, bulk-coordinate variances, and fixed-dimensional feasibility were proved, and the claimed small-aspect-ratio coefficients were recovered algebraically under the missing uniform remainder.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every fixed bulk coordinate \(k>1\), the fixed-dimensional gradient influence variances are rigorously
\[
 s_T=\frac18,
 \qquad s_E=\frac1{16},
 \qquad s_D=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]
The common local negative Hessian is \(\lambda I_p/4\), and \(g(r)=r^2/8+o(r^2)\).  Therefore, if a proportional deterministic equivalent admits a remainder uniform as \(\kappa\downarrow0\), its algebraic first-order coefficient must be
\[
 r_j=\frac{2s_j}{\lambda}\kappa+o(\kappa),
\]
which gives the three coefficients in the target.  The required interchange between the proportional limit and \(\kappa\downarrow0\) is not implied by fixed-dimensional asymptotic linearity.
